findings.title: The profiles x^n do not decay uniformly on [0,1)
findings.explanation: The proof’s intended uniform estimate would require that for every ε>0 there is one N such that y^n<ε for all y∈[0,1) and all n≥N. This is false. For ε=1/2 and any proposed N≥1, choose y with 2^{-1/N}<y<1 and take n=N. Then y^N>1/2. Equivalently, sup_{y∈[0,1)}y^n=1 for every n. Thus the pointwise result R1 cannot support T0.
evidence: R1 gives only a threshold N_x depending on x.
P3 says, ‘Thus the defining uniform estimate holds.’
T0 claims that (a_n) is uniformly attenuating on I.
findings.counterexample: Let ε=1/2. For every proposed N≥1, take n=N and any y∈(2^{-1/N},1). Then y∈I but a_N(y)=y^N>1/2.

findings.title: Boundedness of [0,1) does not justify a finite subcover
findings.explanation: P2 infers that a finite subcover can be chosen because I is a bounded interval. Boundedness alone does not imply compactness, and [0,1) is not compact. Hence U5 and the maximum N=max_j N_{x_j} are not established. For example, the relative-open cover U_k=[0,1-1/k), k≥2, covers [0,1) but has no finite subcover.
evidence: P2 states: ‘Since I is a bounded interval, choose a finite subcover.’
D1 specifies the noncompact interval I=[0,1).
U5 is the resulting asserted finite cover, and D2/U6 form a maximum over that finite family.
P3 provides no further justification beyond ‘Thus the defining uniform estimate holds.’
findings.counterexample: The sets U_k=[0,1-1/k) for k≥2 are open in the subspace [0,1), cover [0,1), and admit no finite subcover.

dispositions.explanation: D1 identifies a_n(x)=x^n on [0,1), and P3 identifies the target as a uniform estimate. The estimate fails by choosing points arbitrarily close to 1 for each proposed uniform threshold.

finding.title: The profiles x^n do not decay uniformly on [0,1)
finding.explanation: For ε=1/2, every proposed N fails at n=N for some y sufficiently close to 1.

dispositions.explanation: The exact source confirms that P2 invokes only boundedness to select a finite subcover. This implication is invalid for I=[0,1), which is not compact.

finding.title: Boundedness of [0,1) does not justify a finite subcover
finding.explanation: P2 incorrectly uses boundedness as a finite-subcover property.
finding.counterexample: The relative-open cover {[0,1-1/k): k≥2} has no finite subcover.

dispositions.explanation: P3 merely asserts that the uniform estimate follows. Its recovered support runs through the finite-cover construction, whose key inference at P2 is invalid; moreover, the asserted estimate is directly false by F1.

finding.title: The conclusion asserted at P3 is false
finding.explanation: P3 cannot establish the uniform estimate because that estimate fails for x^n on [0,1).
finding.counterexample: For ε=1/2 and any N, choose y∈(2^{-1/N},1) and n=N.
